The forward plan is distinct from retrospective coverage; incident attestation is an alternative to a reportable-incident list, with lessons conditional on incidents. This excluded playbook retains the source context without assertions or an implementation checklist. Definition comparison (context only where not invoked by this selected rule): Accepted Vulnerability includes both intentional non-remediation and exceeding the maximum overdue period; the report input register must not be limited to formally signed risk acceptances. All Necessary Parties always includes FedRAMP and every using agency customer, with additional agreement-dependent parties. Prospective customers and third-party providers are usually encouraged but not universally mandatory; roster reconciliation preserves that distinction. Certification Data includes all initial/ongoing certification information, including the package; publication/history references are not reduced to package files alone. Certification Package is the essential authorization-decision information, not just the overview or one evidence file; setup and completeness reviews use that broader boundary. Reportable incidents concern actual or likely confidentiality/integrity effects on federal customer data; a supported no-reportable-incident attestation is not a claim of no operational incidents whatsoever. Likely is a reasonable contextual probability, not certainty or a mandated numerical probability; disclosure and risk findings need reasoned context. MAY is truly optional and documentation is SHOULD; the draft allows non-election while preserving any explicit conditions and embedded MUST clauses. MUST is an absolute requirement, including security-documentation treatment; recommended implementation mechanics do not weaken the official obligation. MUST NOT is an absolute prohibition with security-documentation treatment, not a discretionary risk acceptance. OCR is the regular provider report supplied to agency customers under CCM; a sample shows intended content but not actual reporting history. Quarterly Review is a regular synchronous provider-hosted meeting for agency customers; an asynchronous report is not interchangeable with it. Regularly means consistent, predictable, repeated intervals following a documented plan; evidence of one event cannot establish a recurring cycle. Responsibly means sound independent judgment and cautions against adversary-helpful detail, pre-remediation vulnerability disclosure and compromise-enabling technical detail. Release review is content-specific, not merely approval by title. Security Category concerns FIPS 199 confidentiality/integrity/availability impact, not the A-D certification assurance class; agency ATO context and overview flows retain this distinction. SHOULD permits justified departures only with understood, carefully weighed implications and mandatory documented decisions; the completion criteria preserve this distinction. SHOULD NOT likewise permits justified exceptions with weighed implications and mandatory documented treatment, rather than silently equaling MUST NOT.

The actionable assertions retain the selected official context: Providers MAY responsibly supply some or all of the information an Ongoing Certification Report to the public or other parties if the provider determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering. Definition comparison (context only where not invoked by this selected rule): Accepted Vulnerability includes both intentional non-remediation and exceeding the maximum overdue period; the report input register must not be limited to formally signed risk acceptances. All Necessary Parties always includes FedRAMP and every using agency customer, with additional agreement-dependent parties. Prospective customers and third-party providers are usually encouraged but not universally mandatory; roster reconciliation preserves that distinction. Certification Data includes all initial/ongoing certification information, including the package; publication/history references are not reduced to package files alone. Certification Package is the essential authorization-decision information, not just the overview or one evidence file; setup and completeness reviews use that broader boundary. Reportable incidents concern actual or likely confidentiality/integrity effects on federal customer data; a supported no-reportable-incident attestation is not a claim of no operational incidents whatsoever. Likely is a reasonable contextual probability, not certainty or a mandated numerical probability; disclosure and risk findings need reasoned context. MAY is truly optional and documentation is SHOULD; the draft allows non-election while preserving any explicit conditions and embedded MUST clauses. MUST is an absolute requirement, including security-documentation treatment; recommended implementation mechanics do not weaken the official obligation. MUST NOT is an absolute prohibition with security-documentation treatment, not a discretionary risk acceptance. OCR is the regular provider report supplied to agency customers under CCM; a sample shows intended content but not actual reporting history. Quarterly Review is a regular synchronous provider-hosted meeting for agency customers; an asynchronous report is not interchangeable with it. Regularly means consistent, predictable, repeated intervals following a documented plan; evidence of one event cannot establish a recurring cycle. Responsibly means sound independent judgment and cautions against adversary-helpful detail, pre-remediation vulnerability disclosure and compromise-enabling technical detail. Release review is content-specific, not merely approval by title. Security Category concerns FIPS 199 confidentiality/integrity/availability impact, not the A-D certification assurance class; agency ATO context and overview flows retain this distinction. SHOULD permits justified departures only with understood, carefully weighed implications and mandatory documented decisions; the completion criteria preserve this distinction. SHOULD NOT likewise permits justified exceptions with weighed implications and mandatory documented treatment, rather than silently equaling MUST NOT.

The no-likely-adverse-effect determination is preserved without importing the recording rule's universal agency-information-removal condition. CCM-QTR-SRR: The MAY is conditional on BOTH removing all agency information and determining no likely adverse effect. Independent focused checks retain comments/questions as well as names, across released recording or transcript.  The provider narrative emphasizes effectiveness and resourced security/engineering work; the recommended workflow is a means to demonstrate the specific outcome, not an official extra product or document mandate.
